medaille-dor.heading: 3.—MÉDAILLE D'OR
medaille-dor.flavour: Flesh: yellowish and tender. Juice: very sweet, with a strong, rough, astringent flavour, and not unpleasant.
medaille-dor.quality: As a vintage fruit it takes the very highest rank.
medaille-dor.note: One of the eight Normandy cider apples introduced by the Woolhope Club in 1884 (Appendix to the General Introduction, Plate LXXVII); raised by M. Goddard of Boisguillaume, gold medal 1873.

michelin.heading: 5.—MICHELIN
michelin.flavour: Flesh : white, tender, sweet, and rich.
michelin.quality: This is an apple of the highest merit
michelin.note: Normandy cider apple introduced by the Woolhope Club in 1884; seedling of M. Legrand, Yvetot, first fruited 1872. The verdict is M. Hauchecorne's, quoted.

foxwhelp-broxwood.heading: THE FOX-WHELP APPLE
foxwhelp-broxwood.flavour: Flesh yellow tinged with red, tender, and with a rough and acid flavour.
foxwhelp-broxwood.quality: The Fox-whelp, beyond all question, is the most valuable cider apple
foxwhelp-broxwood.climate: The home of the Fox-whelp Apple, be its origin what it may, is in the deep clay loam of the Old Red Sandstone in the central districts of Herefordshire
foxwhelp-broxwood.note: This is the old Foxwhelp itself (Plate I), not the 20th-century Broxwood selection; recorded as the parent type. The cider is described as 'rough and strong, with a peculiar vinous musky flavour'. Plate VIII describes the Rejuvenated, Bastard, Red and Black Foxwhelps separately.

devonshire-quarrenden.heading: 4. DEVONSHIRE QUARRENDEN
devonshire-quarrenden.flavour: Flesh ; white tinged with green, crisp, brisk, and very juicy, with a rich vinous and refreshing flavour.
devonshire-quarrenden.quality: A very valuable and first-rate dessert apple.
devonshire-quarrenden.storage: It ripens on the tree in the first week of August, and lasts till the end of September.
devonshire-quarrenden.climate: It succeeds well in almost every soil and situation, and is admirably adapted for orchard planting.
devonshire-quarrenden.note: Syn. Quarrington; Red Quarrenden; Sack Apple.

worcester-pearmain.heading: 6. WORCESTER PEARMAIN
worcester-pearmain.flavour: Flesh ; very tender, crisp, juicy, sweet and sprightly, with a very pleasant flavour.
worcester-pearmain.quality: The great beauty of the fruit, and its usefulness, both for dessert and culinary purposes, cannot fail to render it a general favourite.
worcester-pearmain.storage: It is ripe in August and September.
worcester-pearmain.note: Raised at St. John's Nurseries, Worcester, by Richard Smith; first-class certificate 1874.

kerry-pippin.heading: 7. KERRY PIPPIN
kerry-pippin.flavour: Flesh; yellowish white, firm, crisp, and very juicy, with a rich, sugary, brisk and aromatic flavour.
kerry-pippin.quality: an early dessert apple of the highest excellence
kerry-pippin.storage: It is in season during September and October.

stirling-castle.heading: 3. STIRLING CASTLE
stirling-castle.flavour: Flesh ; white, very tender, juicy, and of the character of that of Hawthornden.
stirling-castle.quality: An excellent culinary apple; "a gem of apples" a Herefordshire grower calls it
stirling-castle.storage: It may be used in August and September but is best in flavour from October to December.

keswick-codlin.heading: 1. KESWICK CODLIN
keswick-codlin.flavour: Flesh ; pale yellowish white, very juicy, tender and soft, with a brisk and pleasant flavour, but becomes mealy after being kept for a month. ... It is an apple of fine tartness and flavour
keswick-codlin.quality: One of the most valuable of our early culinary apples
keswick-codlin.storage: becomes mealy after being kept for a month
keswick-codlin.climate: It flourishes best in a strong soil.
keswick-codlin.note: 'fine tartness' and the soil remark are Sir John Sinclair's, quoted.

manks-codlin.heading: 2. MANX CODLIN
manks-codlin.flavour: Flesh ; yellowish white, firm, brisk, juicy and slightly perfumed.
manks-codlin.quality: A very valuable early culinary apple of first-rate quality.
manks-codlin.storage: It is ripe in the beginning of August and continues in use till November.
manks-codlin.climate: It is well suited for planting in exposed situations, and succeeds well in shallow soils.
manks-codlin.note: Syn. Irish Pitcher; Irish Codlin; Eve; Frith Pippin?

lord-suffield.heading: 3. LORD SUFFIELD
lord-suffield.flavour: Flesh ; white, tender and firm, very juicy and briskly flavoured.
lord-suffield.quality: This apple has become the first favourite for early kitchen use
lord-suffield.storage: It is in season in August and September.
lord-suffield.note: Raised by Thomas Thorpe, Middleton, near Manchester; the skin is too fine to travel without bruising.

hawthornden.heading: 4. HAWTHORNDEN
hawthornden.flavour: Flesh; white, crisp and tender, very juicy, with an agreeable and pleasant flavour.
hawthornden.quality: The Hawthornden has long been one of the most valuable and popular apples in cultivation.
hawthornden.storage: It is suitable only for kitchen use, and is in season from October to December.
hawthornden.climate: varying very much in size according to the soil, situation, or condition of the tree
hawthornden.note: Syn. Hawthorndean; White Hawthorndean; Red Hawthorndean. Notes that in some situations it has lately produced small and diseased fruit.

tom-putt.heading: 5. TOM PUTT
tom-putt.flavour: Flesh; white, very tender, sweet and with a pleasant acidity. ... An excellent culinary apple, juicy and high flavoured, when ripe it exudes a pleasant and powerful fragrance
tom-putt.storage: It is in season from September till November.
tom-putt.note: Heading line lost in the OCR (name from the plate caption, Plate VI no. 5); Syn. Tom Potter (Devonshire). Vol. 2's cider list cross-refers 'Marrow-bone, or Tom Putt (see Plate vi)'.

blenheim-orange.heading: BLENHEIM ORANGE
blenheim-orange.flavour: Flesh, yellow, crisp, juicy, sweet and pleasantly acid.
blenheim-orange.quality: A very valuable and highly esteemed apple, either for dessert or culinary purposes, but strictly speaking more suitable for the kitchen than the parlour
blenheim-orange.storage: It is in season from November to February.
blenheim-orange.note: Syn. Blenheim Pippin; Kempster's Pippin; Woodstock Pippin; Northwick Pippin.

dymock-red.heading: 5. DYMOCK RED
dymock-red.flavour: Flesh, yellowish, tender and soft, occasionally tinged with red, slightly sweet, and with a pleasant acidity.
dymock-red.quality: The Cider made from this Apple, whether pure, or mixed with other fruit, is rich and excellent.
dymock-red.note: Cider apple of Dymock, Gloucestershire, probably late 17th century; esteemed in Evelyn's time.

tower-of-glamis.heading: TOWER OF GLAMMIS
tower-of-glamis.flavour: Flesh, greenish white, very juicy, crisp, brisk, and perfumed.
tower-of-glamis.storage: in season from November to February.
tower-of-glamis.note: Syn. Glammis Castle; Gowrie; Carse of Gowrie.

hereford-redstreak.heading: 1. REDSTREAK
hereford-redstreak.flavour: Flesh, yellow, firm, crisp, and rather dry. ... Its cider, though sweet and pleasant, had not much strength, and would not keep well.
hereford-redstreak.quality: As a distinct variety the Redstreak has now ceased to exist, and it may be added that the loss is not to be lamented.
hereford-redstreak.note: Syn. Scudamore's Crab; Herefordshire Redstreak; Redstrake of King's Caple. Lord Scudamore's Redstreak; the book says only one true tree remained (at Kempley). The 'sweet' tag rests on the cider, not the raw fruit.

emperor-alexander.heading: 1. EMPEROR ALEXANDER
emperor-alexander.flavour: Flesh, yellowish white, tender, crisp, juicy, and sugary, with a pleasant and slightly aromatic flavour.
emperor-alexander.quality: This is one of the most beautiful and valuable apples, both as regards its size and quality.
emperor-alexander.storage: It is in season from September to December.
emperor-alexander.climate: The size of its fruit renders protection from the wind desirable.
emperor-alexander.note: Syn. Aporta; Alexander; Russian Emperor. More adapted for culinary than dessert use.

coxs-pomona.heading: 2. COX'S POMONA
coxs-pomona.flavour: Flesh, white, tender, delicate and pleasantly acid.
coxs-pomona.quality: A first-rate and very handsome culinary apple.

beauty-of-kent.heading: 4. BEAUTY OF KENT
beauty-of-kent.flavour: Flesh, yellowish, tender, and juicy, with a pleasant subacid flavour.
beauty-of-kent.quality: A valuable and well-known culinary apple
beauty-of-kent.storage: in season from October to February.
beauty-of-kent.climate: It has a tendency to canker if not in congenial soil
beauty-of-kent.note: Said to be probably the Rambour Franc of the French.

adams-pearmain.heading: 3. ADAMS' PEARMAIN
adams-pearmain.flavour: Flesh, yellow, crisp, juicy, and sugary, with an agreeable and pleasantly perfumed flavour.
adams-pearmain.quality: A dessert apple, of first-rate quality
adams-pearmain.storage: in season from December to February.
adams-pearmain.note: Syn. Norfolk Pippin; Hanging Pearmain; Lady's Finger.

ducks-bill.heading: 6. DUCK'S BILL
ducks-bill.flavour: Flesh, yellowish, firm, crisp, juicy and sugary, with a brisk, piquant, and very pleasant flavour.
ducks-bill.quality: This highly esteemed apple is chiefly suited for culinary purposes, but can take its place on the dessert table with credit
ducks-bill.storage: It is in season from December to April or May.
ducks-bill.note: Syn. Sussex Winter Pearmain; Sussex Scarlet Pearmain. Same entry recorded for winter-pearmain (our aka lists the Sussex names).

winter-pearmain.heading: 6. DUCK'S BILL
winter-pearmain.flavour: Flesh, yellowish, firm, crisp, juicy and sugary, with a brisk, piquant, and very pleasant flavour.
winter-pearmain.quality: This highly esteemed apple is chiefly suited for culinary purposes, but can take its place on the dessert table with credit
winter-pearmain.storage: It is in season from December to April or May.
winter-pearmain.note: Matched through our aka Sussex Duck's Bill / Sussex Scarlet Pearmain. The book says it is 'sometimes locally called Winter Pearmain, but is quite distinct from the Old Winter Pearmain of other parts of the country' - our record mixes the two (it also lists English Winter Pearmain and Winter Quoining). Same lines as ducks-bill.

coxs-orange-pippin.heading: 2. COX'S ORANGE PIPPIN
coxs-orange-pippin.flavour: Flesh : yellowish, very tender in the grain, crisp, juicy and sweet, with a fine perfume.
coxs-orange-pippin.quality: This beautiful apple is the best modern addition to the dessert table ; excellent in flavour, and very handsome.
coxs-orange-pippin.storage: It is in season from October to February.
coxs-orange-pippin.note: Said to be from a pip of the Ribston Pippin, raised 1830 at Colnbrook Lawns.

ecklinville.heading: 1. ECKLINVILLE SEEDLING
ecklinville.flavour: Flesh : white, tender and full grained, with a brisk acidulous flavour.
ecklinville.quality: This is an excellent and handsome culinary apple
ecklinville.storage: in season from October to Christmas.

irish-peach.heading: 2. IRISH PEACH
irish-peach.flavour: Flesh : greenish white, tender, and crisp, abounding in a rich, brisk, vinous and aromatic juice, which at this season is particularly refreshing. ... It has an abundance of rich refreshing juice, and is so sweet, that it readily ferments on the ground
irish-peach.quality: An early dessert apple of the finest quality.
irish-peach.storage: It is ripe during the first week in August and lasts all through that month.

sam-young.heading: 2. SAM YOUNG
sam-young.flavour: Flesh : yellow, tinged with green, firm, crisp, tender, juicy, sugary, and highly flavoured.
sam-young.quality: A delicious little dessert apple of the first quality
sam-young.storage: in season from November to February.

golden-knob.heading: 4. GOLDEN KNOB
golden-knob.flavour: Flesh : firm, with a brisk, juicy, sweet and pleasant flavour.
golden-knob.quality: A good late keeping dessert apple
golden-knob.storage: in season from December to March.

nonpareil.heading: 5. OLD NONPAREIL
nonpareil.flavour: Flesh : greenish white, delicate, crisp, rich, and juicy, abounding in a particularly rich, vinous, and aromatic flavour.
nonpareil.quality: One of the most highly esteemed and popular of all our dessert apples.
nonpareil.storage: It is in season from January to May.
nonpareil.climate: In the Northern counties and in Scotland it does not succeed as a standard, and when grown there under the protection of a wall the fruit is wanting in the fine delicate rich flavour of that grown for the South.
nonpareil.note: Syn. Nonpareil; English Nonpareil; Hunt's Nonpareil; Reinette Nonpareil; Nonpareil d'Angleterre.

braddick-nonpareil.heading: 7. BRADDICK'S NONPAREIL
braddick-nonpareil.flavour: Flesh : yellowish, rich, sugary, and aromatic. One of the best winter dessert apples, and by many considered more sweet and tender than the Old Nonpareil.
braddick-nonpareil.quality: One of the best winter dessert apples
braddick-nonpareil.storage: It is in season from November to April.

lodgemore-nonpareil.heading: 8. LODGEMORE NONPAREIL
lodgemore-nonpareil.flavour: Flesh : yellowish, firm, crisp, juicy, sweet, and with a fine aroma.
lodgemore-nonpareil.quality: A dessert apple of great excellence, and one of the very best late sorts.
lodgemore-nonpareil.storage: It is in season from February to June or even July.

ross-nonpareil.heading: 9. ROSS NONPAREIL
ross-nonpareil.flavour: Flesh : greenish white, firm, crisp, brisk and sugary, charged with a rich and aromatic flavour.
ross-nonpareil.quality: This is one of the richest flavoured dessert apples.
ross-nonpareil.climate: The tree is very hardy and succeeds well upon most soils

warners-king.heading: 1. WARNER'S KING
warners-king.flavour: Flesh : white, tender, crisp, and juicy, with a fine brisk and subacid flavour.
warners-king.quality: A fine, handsome, culinary apple, of first-rate quality.
warners-king.storage: It is in season from November to March.
warners-king.note: Syn. King Apple; Salopian; D. T. Fish; Nelson's Glory; Weavering; Killick's Apple.

golden-noble.heading: 2. GOLDEN NOBLE
golden-noble.flavour: Flesh : yellow, tender, with a pleasant acid juice, perfectly melting, with a rich acidity, and baking of a clear amber colour.
golden-noble.quality: A very attractive and valuable apple, in season from the end of September to the middle of December, and the best in its season.
golden-noble.storage: in season from the end of September to the middle of December

ribston-pippin.heading: 1. RIBSTON PIPPIN
ribston-pippin.flavour: Flesh : yellow, firm, crisp, rich and sugary, and charged with a powerful aromatic flavour.
ribston-pippin.quality: This delicious Apple needs no encomium.
ribston-pippin.storage: It is in greatest perfection during the months of November and December, but with good management it will keep until March.
ribston-pippin.climate: The tree is hardy and vigorous in growth, and bears well when grown in a light, rich and dry soil. It is otherwise apt to canker. ... in the North and in Scotland it requires the protection of a wall to bring it to perfection.
ribston-pippin.note: Syn. Glory of York; Travers Pippin. Long history of the original tree at Ribston Hall.

darcy-spice.heading: 2. D'ARCY SPICE
darcy-spice.flavour: Flesh: greenish white, firm, crisp, juicy, sugary and with a particularly rich and vinous flavour, partaking somewhat of the Ribston and Nonpareil, but particularly of the former.
darcy-spice.quality: This is a dessert apple of first-rate character
darcy-spice.storage: in season from November, but possessing the desirable property of keeping well till April or May.
darcy-spice.note: Syn. Baddow Pippin; Spring Ribston. The entry does not mention spice.

sturmer-pippin.heading: 3. STURMER PIPPIN
sturmer-pippin.flavour: Flesh : yellow, firm, crisp, very juicy, with a brisk and rich sugary flavour.
sturmer-pippin.quality: This is one of the most valuable dessert Apples of its season : it is of first rate excellence
sturmer-pippin.storage: The period of its perfection is from February to June.
sturmer-pippin.note: Said to be Ribston Pippin x Nonpareil.

arbroath-pippin.heading: 1. OSLIN
arbroath-pippin.flavour: Flesh : yellowish, firm, crisp and juicy, rich and sugary, with a highly aromatic flavour, which is peculiar to this apple.
arbroath-pippin.quality: A dessert apple of the highest excellence
arbroath-pippin.storage: ripe by the end of August, and continues through September, but does not last long.
arbroath-pippin.climate: it will ripen in a worse climate and a worse aspect
arbroath-pippin.note: Heading line lost in the OCR; the entry opens with the synonym list (Orglon; Orgeline; Arbroath Pippin; Original Pippin; Mother Apple; Golden Apple; Burr knot; Summer Oslin) and the vol. 2 index names it Oslin / Arbroath Pippin on Plate XXVII. Climate remark quoted from Nichol.

duchess-of-oldenburg.heading: 4. BOROVITSKY
duchess-of-oldenburg.flavour: Flesh : yellowish white, firm, crisp and very juicy, with a pleasant, brisk and refreshing flavour.
duchess-of-oldenburg.quality: An excellent early dessert apple of the first quality
duchess-of-oldenburg.storage: in season from the middle of August, to the end of September.
duchess-of-oldenburg.note: Syn. Duchess of Oldenburgh; Smith's Beauty of Newark; New Brunswick? Sent from the Taurida Gardens, St Petersburg, in 1824.

cider-ladys-finger.heading: 5. CIDER LADY'S FINGER
cider-ladys-finger.flavour: Flesh : yellowish, rather dry ; juice of a fine rich colour, with a sweet subacid and astringent flavour.
cider-ladys-finger.quality: This Apple is a valuable addition to the orchard.
cider-ladys-finger.note: Its cider is described as 'rich, strong, and brisk'.

gennet-moyle.heading: 6. GENNET MOYLE
gennet-moyle.flavour: Flesh : with a yellowish tinge, tender, not very juicy, but rather dry, and with a very sweet, slightly acid flavour. ... This sweet and fragrant apple
gennet-moyle.quality: this Fruit makes the best Cyder in my Judgment
gennet-moyle.storage: The best Baking apple that grows ; and it keeps long baked ; but not so unbaked without growing mealy.
gennet-moyle.climate: Our Gennet Moyles are commonly found in hedges, or in our worst soil, most commonly in Irchenfield, or towards Wales, where the land is somewhat dry and shallow. This Fruit is nice and apt to be discouraged by Blasts
gennet-moyle.note: Not tagged honey: the 'sweetest honey'd Taste' is from the Philips epigraph (verse) printed at the head of the entry. Quality and climate are Dr Beale (1656) quoted; storage is Evelyn quoted.

foxwhelp.heading: THE FOX-WHELP APPLE
foxwhelp.flavour: Flesh yellow tinged with red, tender, and with a rough and acid flavour.
foxwhelp.quality: The Fox-whelp Apple is the favourite cider Apple of Herefordshire.
foxwhelp.note: The old Foxwhelp (Plate I), first recorded by Evelyn 1664, 'of the Forest of Deane'. Juice 'strongly acidulated'. Vol. 1 also has REJUVENATED FOXWHELP (line 17364), which the book thinks is the old variety regrafted ('a piquant acid rough flavour'), plus Bastard, Red and Black Foxwhelp seedlings - not recorded here.

edelborsdorfer.heading: BORSDORFFER
edelborsdorfer.flavour: Flesh ; white with a yellowish tinge, crisp, and delicate, brisk, juicy, and sugary ; and with a rich, vinous, and aromatic flavour.
edelborsdorfer.quality: The Borsdorffer is a dessert apple of the first quality
edelborsdorfer.storage: in season from November to January.
edelborsdorfer.climate: The bloom is also very hardy, and withstands the night frosts of spring better than most other varieties.
edelborsdorfer.note: Synonyms include Queen's Apple and Reinette d'Allemagne as in our aka; Cordus 1561 praised its 'sweet and generous flavour' and 'pleasant perfume'.

gloria-mundi.heading: GLORIA MUNDI
gloria-mundi.flavour: Flesh, white, tender, and juicy, but not highly flavoured.
gloria-mundi.quality: It is an excellent culinary apple
gloria-mundi.storage: in season from October to December.
gloria-mundi.climate: It grows best on a standard, but requires a sheltered situation, to prevent the heavy fruit from being blown off by the wind.
gloria-mundi.note: The heading line is lost in the OCR (Plate X); the entry starts at the synonym line: Baltimore, Belle Dubois, Mammoth, Monstrous Pippin, Ox Apple.

potts-seedling.heading: POTTS' SEEDLING
potts-seedling.flavour: Flesh, white, with a very agreeable acidity.
potts-seedling.quality: This is an excellent cooking apple.
potts-seedling.storage: It is in its best flavour in October and November, but it will keep, with care, until January.
potts-seedling.note: Raised from seed of an American apple at Ashton-under-Lyne about 1849 by Samuel Potts.

cellini.heading: CELLINI
cellini.flavour: Flesh, white, tender, very juicy, brisk and pleasantly flavoured, with a somewhat balsamic aroma.
cellini.quality: its chief use is as a culinary apple of the first quality.
cellini.storage: It is in season during October and November.
cellini.note: Originated with Leonard Phillips of Vauxhall; 'resembling the Nonsuch, from which it was probably raised'.

manningtons-pearmain.heading: MANNINGTON'S PEARMAIN
manningtons-pearmain.flavour: Flesh, yellow, firm, crisp, juicy, and very sugary, with a brisk and particularly rich flavour.
manningtons-pearmain.quality: This is one of the best and richest flavoured dessert apples
manningtons-pearmain.storage: in season from November even till March. The fruit should be allowed to hang late on the tree to secure its richness of flavour, and its good keeping properties, for if gathered too soon it is apt to shrivel.

golden-harvey.heading: GOLDEN HARVEY
golden-harvey.flavour: Flesh : yellow, firm, crisp, juicy, sugary, with an exceedingly rich and powerful aromatic flavour.
golden-harvey.quality: in a warm and favourable season, is perhaps the most delicious of all dessert apples.
golden-harvey.storage: It is fit for the table from December to May or June, but it requires however to be carefully kept, in jars, or in boxes in sand, for if exposed to light and air it will shrivel
golden-harvey.climate: in a warm and favourable season, is perhaps the most delicious of all dessert apples.
golden-harvey.note: Synonyms Round Russet Harvey, Brandy Apple as in our aka. 'The juice is singularly rich and aromatic'; Knight found its specific gravity 1085, the highest he examined.

fenouillet-gris.heading: CARAWAY RUSSET
fenouillet-gris.flavour: Flesh : yellowish, firm, crisp, rich, juicy and sweet, with a fine aroma.
fenouillet-gris.quality: A dessert apple of great excellence
fenouillet-gris.storage: in season from November to February.
fenouillet-gris.note: Caraway Russet is our aka; Bunyard (citing this very page) gives Fenouillet Gris as its correct name. No mention of aniseed here.
